title: app-riset-pdp: Client-Side Face Detection Benchmarking Instrument (OpenCV.js vs face-api.js)
description:
A self-contained, client-side face detection benchmarking instrument built as a single HTML/JavaScript page, with no build step and no server-side dependency. The instrument compares two in-browser face detection pipelines — OpenCV.js (Haar Cascade detector, LBP histogram feature extraction, cosine similarity verification, threshold >= 0.85) and face-api.js (TinyFaceDetector, 68-point facial landmarks, 128-D descriptor, euclidean distance verification, threshold <= 0.60) — under a controlled laboratory experiment with a full 36-scenario factorial design: 3 lighting levels (100, 300, 500 lux) x 4 face pose angles (0, 15, 30, 45 degrees) x 3 device tiers (low-end, mid-range, high-end).

The tool provides: identity enrollment (5/10/15 sample frames per identity, dual-engine registration); manual per-trial testing and an automated 36-scenario runner (1/3/5 trials per scenario) with optional manual-confirmation gating between scenarios so operators can physically change lighting/pose/device conditions; live per-engine metrics (latency in ms, FPS-equivalent, estimated memory usage, trial count); aggregate and per-scenario summary tables (precision, recall, F1-score, average latency); and raw/summary log export in CSV and JSON formats for downstream statistical analysis (Shapiro-Wilk, independent-samples t-test, Mann-Whitney U, three-way ANOVA).

A companion module estimates or measures the server-side processing pathway for comparison against the client-side latency: either by calling a real API endpoint (the companion project api-riset-pdp, deployed as a Cloudflare Worker) or by simulating network conditions (round-trip time, upload/download bandwidth, server processing time) using the model Total = RTT + (payload size x 8 / upload bandwidth) + server processing time + (response size x 8 / download bandwidth).

All biometric processing (face detection, feature extraction, identity verification) executes entirely within the user's browser; no facial image or descriptor data is transmitted off-device during client-side testing, in line with a privacy-by-design architecture. This instrument was developed to collect the experimental data reported in Sismadi, Manan, & Hartini (2026), 'Inovasi Media ICT Deteksi Wajah untuk Presensi Digital Mahasiswa: Analisis Akurasi dan Performa', ACADEMIA: Jurnal Inovasi Riset Akademik, 6(4), 3400-3408, under the Penelitian Dosen Pemula (PDP) research grant at Universitas IPWIJA, Jakarta, involving 50 student participants (n=180 observations per library, closed-set identity verification scenario).
